title: Fallen Heroes Flag Act of 2016
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary has been expanded because action occurred on the measure.)

Fallen Heroes Flag Act of 2016

(Sec. 3) This bill allows the Representative or Senator of an immediate family member of a deceased firefighter, law enforcement officer, member of a rescue squad or ambulance crew, or public safety officer who died in the line of duty to give the family, on request, a Capitol-flown flag, together with a certificate, signed by the official providing the flag (the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the Representative, or the President pro tempore of the Senate and the Senator), that contains an expression of sympathy for the family.

summary.headline: A 2016 law lets members of Congress give Capitol-flown flags and sympathy certificates to families of people who died in the line of duty in public safety jobs.
summary.what_it_does: The law allows a Representative or Senator to give a flag that has flown over the Capitol to the immediate family of a firefighter, police officer, rescue squad or ambulance crew member, or other public safety officer who died in the line of duty. The family must request the flag. The flag comes with a signed certificate that expresses sympathy for the family. The Speaker of the House or the President pro tempore of the Senate signs the certificate, along with the member giving the flag.
summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on May 16, 2016.
